title: Come to the Land of Peace
description: Come to the Land of Peace in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 360, “The Angels' Call”, where the book credits them to Briggs' Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come to the land of peace! From sha-dows come a-way; Where all the sounds of weep-ing cease, And storms no more have sway!

lines: Come to the land of peace!
Where all the sounds of weeping cease,
And storms no more have sway!
Breathe through the bright, celestial air
Come to the bright and blest,
For here thy soul shall find its rest,
Come, trusting spirit, to thy God,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
